primary_rule_source.title: Active Trader interview, March 2004, pp.78–79
primary_rule_source.primary_basis: Direct interview with Raschke, republished by her official website.
primary_rule_source.source_exact: The oscillator subtracts the 10-period simple average from the 3-period simple average. Raschke describes rising price with a falling oscillator as a late-run sell divergence, illustrating a 120-minute chart.

performance_evidence.claim: Her official biography claims her hedge fund ranked 17th among 4,500 for five-year performance in BarclayHedge rankings.
performance_evidence.verification_limit: Self-published claim; underlying ranking and audited return series were not retrieved. The component does not inherit the trader's performance.

zel_operationalization.activation: Only after this lot's first actual profit-only partial fill; never before fill.
zel_operationalization.observation_clock: Native completed 4-hour bars, not the source's illustrated 120-minute chart.
zel_operationalization.indicator: O[j] = SMA3(close)[j] - SMA10(close)[j], using only bars completed by j. Source's additional 16-SMA signal is not used because divergence compares the 3-10 line itself.
zel_operationalization.anchor: Track the largest completed closing price observed since actual entry, with its same-time O reading. Evaluate against the old anchor before updating; equal-price observations do not replace it.
zel_operationalization.trigger: At an eligible post-partial completed bar: close[j] > prior running closing-price high AND O[j] < O_at_that_prior_high. Both oscillator values must be available. No hindsight pivots or future confirmation.
zel_operationalization.execution: Schedule only this lot's remaining quantity at next actual observable open. Preserve existing native-floor/data-safety and original conservative exit priority; an already due source final fill is not duplicated.
explicit_adaptations: Causal running closing-price records formalize the source's discretionary divergence observation.
Source warning becomes a deterministic exit of the existing runner.
4h data and next-open fills follow the frozen ZEL execution model.
unchanged: BE and SMA10 native runner exit

conflicts: Additive runner exit may cut a continuing winner before SMA10; screen must expose that loss.

primary_rule_source.title: TTM Squeeze Indicator Explained
primary_rule_source.primary_basis: Official educational material from the indicator creator's company, with Carter's statements.
primary_rule_source.source_exact: The initial squeeze thrust typically lasts four bars. Unprofitable trades after that initial thrust should be exited before losses grow. This is presented as a tendency and management instruction, not a guaranteed four-bar forecast.

performance_evidence.claim: Creator's company cites a seven-figure TSLA trade and labels Carter an eight-figure trader.
performance_evidence.verification_limit: Company/self-reported promotional claims; no independent broker audit or complete return series was obtained. Weekly trading goals on his plan are not realized performance evidence.

zel_operationalization.activation: One initial-thrust check for each original actual entry campaign; later reuse campaigns receive the same rule independently.
zel_operationalization.observation_clock: Fourth completed native4h bar since actual entry, counting entry bar as completed bar1: j=entry_index+3.
zel_operationalization.mapping: The existing reg71 squeeze/continuation signal is the frozen release event. Do not add a new TTM squeeze or momentum filter.
zel_operationalization.profit_measure: unit_net_progress_bps = 10000*(completed_close/actual_entry_price-1) - frozen cost_at(cost, entry_ts, completed_close_ts). This defines unprofitable after costs rather than gross-price-only.
zel_operationalization.trigger: At that single fourth-bar close, if unit_net_progress_bps <=0 schedule this lot's remaining quantity to exit at the next actual observable open. If positive, disable this component for the rest of that campaign; no later rearm.
zel_operationalization.execution: Native floor, data safety and existing source-exit priority remain. No next actual open before terminal boundary means terminal mark with pending exit, not synthetic liquidation.
explicit_adaptations: An approximate source four-bar thrust becomes a one-time deterministic checkpoint.
The frozen reg71 signal replaces Carter's full TTM entry setup.
Net-of-cost profitability, completed4h clock and next-open fill semantics are ZEL choices fixed before outcomes.
unchanged: D3 profit-only 1/3 partial if the lot survives
BE and SMA10 native runner exit

conflicts: Can terminate before D3; this is the single intended initial-failure axis.
Do not combine the earlier investigated Carter box-return or two-blue-bar ideas into this candidate.
